statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Let h be the maximum depth of a node of root, with the root at depth 0. For each d with 0 <= d <= h, let L_d be the list of values of the nodes at depth d in left-to-right order, let m_d = len(L_d), and let pi_d be the permutation of {0,...,m_d-1} sending i to the number of j with 0 <= j < m_d and L_d[j] < L_d[i]. Let c_d be the number of cycles of pi_d. Then r = sum_{d=0}^{h} (m_d - c_d). Equivalently, r is the minimum total number of same-level swaps needed so that, at every depth d, the values in left-to-right order are strictly increasing.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or run out of bounds on this input.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r >= 0.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r. Let N be the number of Node constructors in root and let h be the maximum depth of a node of root, with the root at depth 0. Then r <= N - (h + 1).
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r. Let h be the maximum depth of a node of root, and for each d with 0 <= d <= h let L_d be the list of values of nodes at depth d in left-to-right order. Then r = 0 if and only if for every d with 0 <= d <= h and every i with 0 <= i < len(L_d) - 1, L_d[i] < L_d[i + 1].
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exists a sequence of exactly r same-level swaps (each swap exchanges the values of two distinct nodes at the same depth) after which every level list of the resulting tree, in left-to-right order, is strictly increasing.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r, and for every k with 0 <= k < r there is no sequence of k same-level swaps (each exchanging the values of two distinct nodes at the same depth) after which every level list of the resulting tree is strictly increasing.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r. Let h be the maximum depth of a node of root, and for each d with 0 <= d <= h let L_d be the list of values of nodes at depth d in left-to-right order. For a list a let inv(a) be the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < len(a) and a[i] > a[j]. Then r mod 2 = (sum_{d=0}^{h} inv(L_d)) mod 2.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns results r1 for root1 and r2 for root2. For a tree t and each d >= 0, let L_d(t) be the list of values of nodes at depth d in left-to-right order. If for every d >= 0 the lists L_d(root1) and L_d(root2) have the same length and, for all i,j with 0 <= i,j < that common length, L_d(root1)[i] < L_d(root1)[j] if and only if L_d(root2)[i] < L_d(root2)[j], then r1 = r2.
preconditions: root1 and root2 are both non-null finite Trees with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value in each tree is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values within root1 are pairwise distinct, and all node values within root2 are pairwise distinct.

statement: The function returns a result r. Let h be the maximum depth of a node of root. Then r is the number of depths d with 0 <= d <= h such that len(L_d(root)) = 2 and L_d(root)[0] > L_d(root)[1].
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct; and for every d >= 0, len(L_d(root)) <= 2, where L_d(root) is the list of values of nodes at depth d in left-to-right order.

statement: The function returns a result r. Let h be the maximum depth of a node of root, and for each d with 0 <= d <= h let L_d be the list of values of nodes at depth d in left-to-right order. For a list a let inv(a) be the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < j < len(a) and a[i] > a[j]. Then r <= sum_{d=0}^{h} inv(L_d).

statement: The function returns a result r. Let h be the maximum depth of a node of root. For each d with 0 <= d <= h, let L_d be the list of values of nodes at depth d in left-to-right order, let m_d = len(L_d), and let c_d be the number of cycles of the permutation of {0,...,m_d-1} sending i to the number of j with 0 <= j < m_d and L_d[j] < L_d[i]. Then r >= m_d - c_d for every such d.
preconditions: root is a non-null finite Tree with at most 100000 nodes; every Node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 100000; all node values in root are pairwise distinct.
